subject.title: refactor: move MCP OAuth state to SQLite

question: Should MCP OAuth upgrades intentionally fail closed until `openclaw doctor --fix` imports legacy credentials, with no runtime JSON fallback and logout tombstones preventing stale-file resurrection?
rationale: This deliberately trades seamless upgrade compatibility for one credential owner and stronger anti-resurrection semantics; code review cannot choose that release and security boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Approve Doctor-only cutover
options.body: Keep SQLite as the only runtime store, require explicit Doctor migration, and accept fail-closed behavior for unresolved legacy state.

options.title: Require transitional compatibility
options.body: Delay merge and design an explicitly approved temporary upgrade path despite the additional dual-owner and stale-credential risk.

options.title: Pause the migration
options.body: Retain the current JSON store until maintainers define a different credential-storage and upgrade contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Doctor-only cutover
recommendation.body: Keep SQLite as the only runtime store, require explicit Doctor migration, and accept fail-closed behavior for unresolved legacy state.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle was explicitly requested to decide the credential migration and authorization boundary.
